hook: Engineers lowered 10 tunnel elements weighing 47,000 tonnes each underwater.

sections.voiceover: Engineers lowered 10 tunnel elements weighing 47,000 tonnes each underwater.
sections.visual_cue: Underwater view of a precast concrete tunnel element being submerged into a deep water channel.
b_roll: Government engineering illustration of submerged concrete tunnel placement

sections.voiceover: Daewoo Engineering & Construction partnered with Ballast Nedam in Basra to build an immersed tunnel. It connects the Faw Peninsula to Umm Qasr. How were 10 elements placed beneath the Khor Al-Zubair?
sections.visual_cue: Map graphic highlighting Basra, the Faw Peninsula, Umm Qasr, and the Khor Al-Zubair waterway.
b_roll: Satellite mapping imagery showing Basra port network and Khor Al-Zubair waterway

sections.voiceover: But Daewoo Engineering & Construction didn't work alone, partnering with Trelleborg Marine & Infrastructure for customized sealing systems.
sections.visual_cue: Technical cross-section diagram of heavy rubber marine gaskets compressing under sea water pressure.
b_roll: Diagram showing specialized marine sealing joints sliding into place

sections.voiceover: Ashtead Technology guided all 10 concrete elements inside the channel. The General Company for Ports of Iraq completed the link. Daewoo secured 9 contracts worth $3.78 billion.
sections.visual_cue: Positioning sensors aligning submerged tunnel segments on the seabed, transitioning to contract figures.
sections.sfx_cue: Heavy metallic locking clack followed by low synth pulse
b_roll: Positioning sonar guidance interface simulation for underwater positioning
Overview of Al Faw Port infrastructure marine works

sections.voiceover: That includes $510 million for the container terminal quay wall.
sections.visual_cue: Architectural rendering of completed container terminal quay wall along the waterfront.
b_roll: Finished container terminal quay wall layout graphic
